question: An 8-day-old male infant presents to the pediatrician with a high-grade fever and poor feeding pattern with regurgitation of milk after each feeding. On examination the infant showed abnormal movements, hypertonia, and exaggerated DTRs. The mother explains that during her pregnancy, she has tried to eat only unprocessed foods and unpasterized dairy so that her baby would not be exposed to any preservatives or unhealthy chemicals. Which of the following characteristics describes the causative agent that caused this illness in the infant?

options.opb: Gram-positive, catalase-negative, beta hemolytic, bacitracin resistant cocci
options.opd: Gram-positive, catalase-negative, alpha hemolytic, optochin sensitive cocci

reasoning_chain: CHAIN: "Unpasteurized dairy consumption" -> "Possible exposure to Listeria monocytogenes" -> "Gram-positive, facultative intracellular, motile bacilli" -> 90%
CHAIN: "High-grade fever in infant" -> "Possible bacterial infection" -> "Listeria monocytogenes" -> "Gram-positive, facultative intracellular, motile bacilli" -> 85%
CHAIN: "Abnormal movements and hypertonia in infant" -> "Central nervous system involvement" -> "Listeria monocytogenes infection" -> "Gram-positive, facultative intracellular, motile bacilli" -> 80%
CHAIN: "Exaggerated DTRs in infant" -> "Neurological symptoms" -> "Listeria monocytogenes" -> "Gram-positive, facultative intracellular, motile bacilli" -> 75%
analysis: The infant's symptoms and the mother's dietary habits suggest a case of neonatal listeriosis. The mother consumed unpasteurized dairy products, which are a common source of Listeria monocytogenes, a bacterium that can cause serious infections in newborns. Listeria monocytogenes is characterized as a Gram-positive, facultative intracellular, motile bacillus. This matches the description in option opa.
